_partNote: Class tiles for ai-compute-and-accelerators, generated 2026-08-19 with `generate-images.js parts`. Subjects were checked against this sheet's own entry list so no tile depicts a subject belonging to a different class. Classes IV and V have no photographable subject, so both use a deliberately abstract geometric stand-in with a silhouette unlike any other tile. The color list below is this domain's own trap set: circuit boards are green, heatsinks and interconnect are copper, racks are black, fiber patch cords are aqua and yellow, and bare silicon wafers are iridescent, and the model will reach for every one of those unless told not to. Installed tiles are the 'a' candidate for all seven classes, from the first two passes, at 900px wide to match the rest of the site. The abstract stand-ins for classes IV and V both worked first time, which is new: previous guidance was that abstract subjects draw badly. What made them work is that each was specified as a real physical arrangement with numeric proportions (a halving staircase of solid blocks, four slabs on corner pillars) rather than as a concept to be interpreted.
style: Minimalist technical illustration, the style of a precise patent drawing crossed with an isometric product sketch. Uniform-weight dark slate-gray ink linework with sparse, muted steel-blue accent shading (hex 4E7AA8) on a plain very light warm-gray background (hex F2F3F1). Three-quarter isometric view, single centered subject, generous margins. No text, no labels, no callouts, no logos, no humans, no background scenery, no drop shadows. Clean, engineered, calm. Strictly two colors plus the background: dark slate-gray line and muted steel-blue fill. The drawing must read as line art, not as a rendered solid model. Absolutely no green circuit-board substrate, no copper, brass, gold or orange metal, no black or dark equipment bodies, no yellow or aqua cable jackets, and no iridescent rainbow wafer sheen, even where the real object would be exactly that color. Every material is drawn in the same two-color palette.

partPrompts.1: A single accelerator add-in board lying flat, seen three-quarter: a long flat rectangular circuit board with a bold finned heatsink covering most of its upper face, the fins drawn as a row of about twelve straight parallel plates running along the length, a plain rectangular bracket at one short end and a row of contact fingers along one long edge. The board is roughly three times longer than it is wide. One bold object filling the frame, simple outline, no components smaller than the fins, no cables, no chassis, no slot, no other boards.
partPrompts.2: A single stack of memory dies standing on a flat square base, seen three-quarter: eight identical thin square plates stacked squarely on top of each other like a short tower of tiles, each plate the same size, with a clearly visible gap line between every plate, standing on one thicker square baseplate. The stack is about as tall as the base is wide. Bold, blocky and obviously layered. No wires, no board, no heatsink, no processor beside it, no cutaway.
partPrompts.3: A single network switch chassis seen three-quarter, with eight cables leaving it: a plain wide rectangular box, about four times wider than it is tall, with a row of small square ports across its front face, and eight smooth cables of equal thickness sweeping out from those ports and away toward the viewer's left and right in broad even curves, each cable ending cleanly in open space. The cables are the dominant feature. No racks, no other equipment, no connectors drawn in detail, no tangle.
partPrompts.4: A set of four solid rectangular gauge blocks standing upright in a row on a flat surface, seen three-quarter, arranged as a descending staircase: the leftmost block is the tallest and widest, and each block to its right is exactly half the height and half the width of the one before it, so the fourth is very small. Blocks are plain solid rectangular prisms with no markings, evenly spaced, all standing on the same flat surface. Bold and unmistakably a halving sequence. No text, no numbers, no ruler, no measuring instrument, no case.
partPrompts.5: Four identical flat rectangular slabs stacked one above the other with a clear air gap between each, seen three-quarter, each slab rotated slightly about the vertical axis relative to the one below so the stack reads as offset layers, with four slender vertical pillars at the corners passing through the whole stack to hold it together. The stack is about as tall as one slab is wide. Bold, clean and obviously layered. No text, no icons, no electronics, no board, no components on the slabs.
partPrompts.6: A row of three identical server racks standing side by side on a flat floor, seen three-quarter: each rack is a tall plain rectangular cabinet, at least three times taller than it is wide, its front face divided into about twelve equal horizontal slots by simple straight lines, standing directly on the floor with no plinth. The three cabinets touch each other in a straight row. Drawn as room-sized equipment rather than as a small part. No cables, no doors, no people, no room, no ceiling, no floor tiles.
partPrompts.7: A single shipping pallet stacked with sealed cartons, seen three-quarter: a plain slatted wooden pallet at the bottom, and on it a block of six identical plain rectangular cartons arranged two deep and three high, the whole load squared off, with two flat strapping bands running around the load, one horizontal near the top and one horizontal near the bottom. The load is about as tall as the pallet is wide. Bold and simple. No text, no labels, no barcodes, no forklift, no warehouse, no shrink wrap.
